milestone: Starting a natural history study for Metachromatic leukodystrophy
why_it_matters: A natural history study records how a disease progresses without treatment. Regulators ask for it before trials.

numbers.basis: Metachromatic leukodystrophy and its close relatives

usual_route: FDA draft guidance says prospective natural history studies generally take more time than reusing existing data, and longitudinal ones can be lengthy and costly.
No published figure was found for the time to set up such a study (protocol, ethics approval, sites, funding), so none is stated.

usual_route_source.label: FDA, Rare Diseases: Natural History Studies for Drug Development (2019)

atlas_route: Metachromatic leukodystrophy already has 4 natural history studies registered. Check these first: joining may beat starting a new one.
1 more exist for Krabbe disease: protocols, outcome measures and teams to learn from and ask to collaborate with.

relative_studies.title: The Natural History of Infantile Globoid Cell Leukodystrophy

assumptions: A study for Metachromatic leukodystrophy could reuse outcome measures from its relatives. Not yet validated: clinicians must confirm the diseases are close enough (shared mechanism, different genes).
Durations are those of the registered studies; a new study could be shorter or longer.
No time or cost saving is stated, because there is no cited figure for one.
validate_next: Whether each existing study is still enrolling and open to families with Metachromatic leukodystrophy.
Whether relatives' protocols and registries can be shared (ask the sponsors).
Expert review of how well outcome measures transfer between these diseases.
